analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Pharmalabs is a decent API/CDMO business with solid earnings growth (30.6% net profit CAGR), but at an earnings yield of ~6.9% and ROIC of ~17-18%, it fails to clear the Magic Formula's dual hurdles of being both cheap AND exceptional. The ongoing capex binge (INR 444 Cr capex vs INR 272 Cr net profit in FY25) makes the business capital-hungry right now, not the cash-generating machine the formula demands.
key_strengths: Strong earnings growth: Net profit CAGR 30.6% and EBITDA CAGR 33.7% over 3 years — the underlying business is compounding well
Diversified API portfolio across 15+ therapeutic areas plus CDMO contracts provides revenue durability
Low leverage (D/E 0.33) and 51.3% gross margin indicate pricing power and manageable financial risk
key_risks: Capex destroying FCF: INR 444 Cr capex in FY25 vs INR 272 Cr net profit, generating -112 Cr free cash flow — the formula hates capital-intensive expansion
Earnings yield of ~6.9% (EBIT 464 Cr / EV ~6,749 Cr) — barely above the 6% floor, nowhere near the 12-15% the Magic Formula targets
Borrowings nearly tripled from INR 215 Cr (FY23) to INR 659 Cr (FY25) — debt is rising fast to fund capex, adding financial risk if expansion doesn't deliver returns
red_flags: FY25 free cash flow: -112 Cr despite INR 272 Cr net profit — capex/net profit ratio of 163% signals low FCF conversion
Earnings yield ~6.9% — below the 12% Magic Formula attractiveness threshold; stock is not cheap on EV basis
ROIC/ROCE of 17.4% is decent but well below the 25%+ Greenblatt benchmark for a 'wonderful business'
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT (Operating Income) of INR 464 Cr against Enterprise Value of ~INR 6,749 Cr (Market Cap 6,335 + Debt 421 - Cash 7) yields an earnings yield of just 6.9% — barely above the 6% avoid threshold and far short of the 12-15% that signals a genuinely cheap stock. ROCE of 17.4% is respectable for an Indian API manufacturer but doesn't reach the 25%+ that would classify this as a truly high-quality compounder. On both dimensions — cheapness and quality — Aarti Pharmalabs lands in the middle of the pack, which is precisely where the Magic Formula generates no alpha.

The growth story is real: revenue up 20.8% CAGR, EBITDA up 33.7% — but the business is in a heavy reinvestment phase. FY25 capex of INR 444 Cr consumed 163% of net profit, producing -112 Cr in free cash flow. The CWIP of INR 160 Cr and surging borrowings (INR 659 Cr, up from INR 215 Cr in FY23) confirm this is a company spending aggressively to build capacity. If that capex generates 20%+ ROIC once commissioned, the story improves — but until FCF turns positive and sustained, this is a speculative growth bet, not a Magic Formula buy. Wait for the capex cycle to mature and re-rate at a lower price.
